prompt.context_jp: 夕暮れの気配が残るオフィスの一角で、里中賢介は大前春子の前に立ちはだかっていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 夕暮れの気配___残るオフィスの一角で…
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits? (describing the dusk still lingering in the office)

feedback.correct_en: This is a descriptive relative clause setting the scene — new, non-topical information. が marks the subject of the subordinate clause 'where dusk's traces remain.'
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make 'dusk's traces' a contrastive topic, which doesn't fit a scene-setting description embedded in a relative clause.

contrast_examples.jp: 雨は降る、雪は降らない
contrast_examples.en: rain falls, but snow doesn't (contrastive topic)

prompt.context_jp: 春子はどの職場でも私情に流されずに数字だけを提示してきた人間だった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 春子___どの職場でも私情に流されずに数字だけを提示してきた人間だった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits for the sentence-level topic 'Haruko'?

feedback.correct_en: The narrator is characterizing Haruko as an established topic — describing what kind of person she is. は marks the thematic subject of a defining statement.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would introduce Haruko as new information or exhaustively identify her, which clashes with the general characterization being given.

contrast_examples.en: She is a calm person. (topic + characterization)
She's the one who is calm. (exhaustive identification)

prompt.context_jp: 九十八回の別れを重ねた女の存在を、里中は初めて意識する場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 一つの職場での別れを九十八回繰り返してきた女___いま目の前に立っていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits? (presenting the woman as a newly-apprehended figure)

feedback.correct_en: The long description introduces a vivid new entity into Satonaka's awareness — classic が of new information / existential presentation.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would treat this heavily-modified noun as an already-known topic, but the point is her striking new-to-him reality.

contrast_examples.jp: 見知らぬ男が立っていた
contrast_examples.en: A stranger was standing there. (new presentation)

prompt.context_jp: 「98社…」と言った春子が、手のひらの数字について説明する。
prompt.prompt_jp: 私___これまで派遣で行った会社の数です。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits? (identifying which number '98' represents)

feedback.correct_en: This is a cleft-like identification: 'that is the number of companies I went to.' The relative-clause subject '私' takes が in an embedded modifier.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would wrongly topicalize '私' across the subordinate clause boundary; in '私___派遣で行った会社' the subject of the inner clause must be が.

prompt.context_jp: 春子が里中を評価する場面。「甘々なところを除けば…」
prompt.prompt_jp: 里中主任___素晴らしい上司です。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits? (giving an evaluative characterization of Satonaka)

feedback.correct_en: Haruko is stating an evaluative judgment about Satonaka as the topic — 'as for Chief Satonaka, he is a wonderful boss.' は fits the characterizing predicate.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would exhaustively pick him out as 'the one who is a wonderful boss,' which isn't her point; she's describing him.

contrast_examples.jp: 田中さんは優しい人です
田中さんが優しい人です

prompt.context_jp: 里中に褒められた直後の春子の返答。
prompt.prompt_jp: でも 私___3か月で去ります。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits? (contrasting her choice against Satonaka's wishes)

feedback.correct_en: 'でも' sets up contrast with his wish that she stay. は marks '私' as a contrastive topic: 'as for me, (regardless) I'm leaving.'
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make it a neutral new-information subject, losing the contrastive pushback that 'でも' demands.

contrast_examples.jp: でも 私は行きません
contrast_examples.en: But I (as for me) am not going.

prompt.context_jp: 3か月以上働くことの弊害を春子が列挙する場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 私のスキル___あまりにも高すぎて 社員との間に格差が生じます。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits? (stating the newly-presented cause within a subordinate reason-clause)

feedback.correct_en: Inside a causal 'て' clause giving a reason, the subject takes が — 'because my skills are too high, a gap emerges.'
feedback.incorrect_en: は would topicalize 'my skills' across the subordinate reason-clause, which sounds unnatural in this cause-stating structure.

contrast_examples.en: The wind is strong, so I can't walk.
The wind is strong, but I can walk. (contrastive main clause)

prompt.context_jp: ナレーションが春子を紹介する一文。
prompt.prompt_jp: 彼女の辞書___ “不可能”と“契約更新”の文字はない。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks '彼女の辞書に' as the thematic locus?

feedback.correct_en: 'には' topicalizes the location (her dictionary) as the frame of discussion: 'in her dictionary, those words don't exist.' This is the standard pattern.
feedback.incorrect_en: 'にが' is ungrammatical — が cannot stack onto に this way in modern Japanese.

contrast_examples.en: In this shop, there's a cat.
There is a cat in this shop. (neutral existence)

prompt.context_jp: 朝礼で里中が発売日を発表する。
prompt.prompt_jp: “ハケン弁当”の発売日___決まりました。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits? (announcing new information)

feedback.correct_en: This is a classic news-announcement: 'The release date has (just) been decided.' The release date is new information presented to the team — が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would imply the release date is already an established topic and you're commenting on it, but the whole point is that it was just set.

contrast_examples.en: The meeting is next week. (topic continuation)

prompt.context_jp: 課員が「森ちゃんと大前さんはいないかも」と言ったのへの春子の返答。
prompt.prompt_jp: “かも”ではなく 私___いません。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits? (correcting 'maybe gone' to 'definitely gone')

feedback.correct_en: Haruko contrasts herself against the 'maybe' framing: 'as for me (whatever Mori does), I won't be here.' は marks the contrastive topic.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would exhaustively say 'I am the one not here,' which sounds odd when she's disputing the modality ('maybe' → definite), not identifying who's absent.

contrast_examples.jp: 他の人は来るが、私は来ない
contrast_examples.en: Others will come, but I won't.

prompt.context_jp: 東海林の「引き止め作戦」。春子はさば味噌が大好きだという話の続き。
prompt.prompt_jp: あいつの体___さば味噌でできている。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits? (characterizing 'her body')

feedback.correct_en: A humorous characterization statement — 'her body (as a topic) is made of mackerel miso.' は for the topic+defining predicate.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would exhaustively identify 'her body' as the thing made of sabamiso, missing the joking generalization he's making about Haruko.

prompt.context_jp: 里中が課に戻って報告する。
prompt.prompt_jp: 部長のＯＫ___取れました！
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits? (excitedly reporting a result just achieved)

feedback.correct_en: He's announcing a fresh accomplishment — new information. が presents '部長のOK' as the newly-obtained thing.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would imply 'as for the director's OK, (we got it, but...)' — setting up a contrast or qualifier, which doesn't match his triumphant report.

contrast_examples.en: As for permission, not yet. (contrastive topic)

prompt.context_jp: ツネさんが若き日の春子について語る。
prompt.prompt_jp: 春ちゃん___両親に早くに死に別れて 独りぼっちだったんだな。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits? (giving background about Haruko as topic)

feedback.correct_en: Tsune is telling Haruko's background story — she is the established topic and he's describing her state. は is standard for this kind of biographical commentary.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would awkwardly re-introduce her as new info, but she's already the person they've been talking about.

prompt.context_jp: 東海林が電話でS&Fに連絡し、春子が出た。
prompt.prompt_jp: 一番 出てほしくないヤツ___出た。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits? (the worst possible person — of all people — picked up)

feedback.correct_en: 'The one I least wanted' is exhaustively picked out — が identifies 'she, of all people' as the one who actually answered.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would topicalize 'the person I didn't want' and sound like a general comment, losing the shocked 'it was HER who answered' punch.

contrast_examples.jp: 一番高いのは売れない
contrast_examples.en: As for the most expensive, it doesn't sell. (contrastive topic)

prompt.context_jp: 春子が森に伝える人生観。
prompt.prompt_jp: 働くこと___生きることです。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits? (defining 'working' = 'living')

feedback.correct_en: This is a classic 'A は B です' definitional/thematic equation: 'Working is living.' は sets '働くこと' as the topic being defined.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would exhaustively identify 'working' as the unique thing that is 'living,' which distorts the aphoristic, equative meaning.

prompt.context_jp: 里中が春子を引き留める、必死の訴え。
prompt.prompt_jp: 行かないでください。僕には あなた___必要なんです。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks 'you' in '僕には〜が必要'?

feedback.correct_en: 必要 (hitsuyou) is an adjectival noun; the needed thing is marked with が: '僕にはあなたが必要だ' = 'I need you.'
feedback.incorrect_en: を would treat 必要 as a verb taking a direct object (it isn't), and に doesn't fit this stative-need construction.

prompt.context_jp: 東海林が名古屋での自分をアピール。
prompt.prompt_jp: ___を得た魚のように バリバリやってるから。
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in the set idiom meaning 'in one's element'.

feedback.correct_en: '水を得た魚' ('a fish getting water') is the fixed idiom for thriving in one's element — exactly what Shoji is claiming (falsely) about Nagoya.
feedback.incorrect_en: 風 or 陸 don't form this idiom; a fish out of water (陸) would mean the opposite of what he's bragging.

contrast_examples.en: A fish on land (out of one's element).

prompt.context_jp: なぜ契約更新しないのかを執拗に問われた春子の返答。
prompt.prompt_jp: こういう質問をされること自体 大きな___です。
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in Haruko's biting retort meaning 'none of your business'.

feedback.correct_en: '大きなお世話' is the set phrase 'that's none of your business / unwanted meddling' — Haruko's signature cutting response.
feedback.incorrect_en: '大きな問題' means 'a big problem' and '大きな迷惑' means 'a huge nuisance,' but neither is the idiomatic brush-off she uses.

prompt.context_jp: 春子が黒岩に塩の値段を説明した後の決め台詞。
prompt.prompt_jp: お弁当の味に影響___出ますが 何か？
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb completes the collocation 影響___出る?

feedback.correct_en: '影響が出る' ('an effect emerges / shows') is the natural intransitive collocation — the subject-marker が goes with the auto-verb 出る.
feedback.incorrect_en: '影響を出す' would require a transitive agent causing the effect, which doesn't fit here where she describes a consequence that would arise.

prompt.context_jp: 一ツ木が森の契約更新を知らせる場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 里中主任が桐島部長や人事部に 熱心に ___くださったそうです。
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in the verb meaning 'negotiated on your behalf'.

feedback.correct_en: '掛け合う' means to negotiate/petition with someone on behalf of a cause — exactly what Satonaka did with the director and HR.
feedback.incorrect_en: '話し合う' is a mutual discussion (too neutral), and '呼びかける' is 'to call out/appeal to (a group).' Neither captures the active petitioning nuance.

prompt.context_jp: ツネさんが里中たちに言う。
prompt.prompt_jp: 最高の さばを ___してやる。
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in the verb: 'I'll procure (the best mackerel) for you.'

feedback.correct_en: '調達する' means 'to procure / source,' the right verb for a market broker arranging supplies.
feedback.incorrect_en: '配達' is 'delivery' (to the end user), and '発達' is 'development' — neither works here.

prompt.context_jp: 東海林が賢ちゃんに名古屋での屈辱を吐露するメール。
prompt.prompt_jp: 耐えがたい___感と屈辱を 味わってるんだ。
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in: 'unbearable sense of ___ and humiliation'.

feedback.correct_en: '疎外感' (sogaikan) = 'alienation / feeling of being excluded,' which matches 'ネクタイ' isolation and pairs with '屈辱'.
feedback.incorrect_en: '安心感' (reassurance) and '満足感' (satisfaction) are positive feelings and contradict the painful context.

prompt.context_jp: 最終出勤日、春子が静かに課を去る。
prompt.prompt_jp: 契約終了しました。お先に___。
prompt.prompt_en: Complete the set workplace farewell.

feedback.correct_en: 'お先に失礼します' is the fixed phrase said when leaving the office before others — the proper, composed goodbye for Haruko.
feedback.incorrect_en: 'お疲れです' is used toward others who have worked, not to announce your own departure. 'ごめんなさい' is a personal apology, out of register.

contrast_examples.en: Thanks for your work. (said to others)

prompt.context_jp: 春子の毅然とした口調で、里中の引き留めを断る場面。
prompt.prompt_en: Which line sounds more like Haruko's characteristic brusque register?

choices.text: でも 私は3か月で去ります。
でも、私は3か月で去っちゃうかもしれません。

feedback.correct_en: Haruko's voice is flat, declarative, and admits no softening. 'で去ります' is clipped and definitive — matches her 'I will be gone' certainty from line 0062.
feedback.incorrect_en: '去っちゃうかもしれません' adds the casual ちゃう + 'maybe' hedge, which clashes with the rule-bound, uncompromising persona she projects.

prompt.context_jp: 質問攻めに対する春子の冷ややかな返し。
prompt.prompt_en: Which closing phrase is more natural in Haruko's cutting style?

choices.text: あと3週間 お時給の分は しっかり働かせていただきます。
あと3週間 お時給の分、ちゃんと働かせてもらいますよ。

feedback.correct_en: The 謙譲 'させていただきます' and particle は for contrast ('at least the hourly wage's worth') match Haruko's ice-cold business politeness.
feedback.incorrect_en: 'もらいますよ' with final よ sounds chatty and defensive, not the detached professional voice she maintains.

contrast_examples.jp: 働かせていただきます

prompt.context_jp: 派遣会社の一ツ木が、里中の尽力を森に伝える。
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing is more natural in a派遣会社's formal report to a worker?

choices.text: 里中主任が 熱心に 掛け合ってくださったそうです。
里中主任が 熱心に 掛け合いをやってくれたらしいです。

feedback.correct_en: '掛け合ってくださった' uses the respectful くださる form appropriate to speaking of a client's manager, and 'そうです' is the formal hearsay form. Smooth business register.
feedback.incorrect_en: 'やってくれた' is too casual and '掛け合いをやる' is a clumsy nominalization — neither fits a staffing agent's polite report.

contrast_examples.en: (He) was kind enough to make the effort. (formal)

prompt.context_jp: 春子が森に贈る、めずらしく温かい労い。
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds more natural as the elder Haruko addressing her junior?

choices.text: あなたが よく ここまで成長しました。
あなたは とても ここまで成長されました。

feedback.correct_en: 'よく〜しました' is the standard warm acknowledgement of someone's growth ('you've done well to make it this far'). Senior-to-junior natural register.
feedback.incorrect_en: 'とても…成長されました' mixes respectful 尊敬語 toward a junior (odd power dynamic) and 'とても' doesn't collocate as naturally as 'よく' for sustained effort.

prompt.context_jp: 大雪で弁当箱が届かず、里中がうめく台詞。
prompt.prompt_en: Which sounds more natural as a dramatic lament?

choices.text: 天は 我々を見放したか…
天は 我々を見放しちゃったか…

feedback.correct_en: '見放したか' is the classic, slightly archaic exclamation of dramatic despair (famously from 八甲田山). The literary register matches the TV-drama cadence.
feedback.incorrect_en: '見放しちゃったか' mixes the solemn '天' with the casual-regret ちゃった, which breaks the dramatic register.
